key_insight: The paper shows that disagreement among LLM agents can be resolved more reliably by comparing forward and Bayesian backward posteriors, using their cross-path consistency as a label-free anchor for aggregation.
engineering_relevance: For multi-agent AI systems, this offers a practical way to improve ensemble decision-making without extra labels, especially when agents make correlated errors under the same evidence.
method: Build a reverse posterior via Bayesian backward reasoning from an explicit likelihood.
Measure Jensen–Shannon divergence between forward and reverse posteriors to rank agents by consistency.
Use this signal for hard selection (MinJS), soft reweighting (FwdJS), or log-linear fusion (LogLin).
evidence_signal: Across DDXPlus and five LLM backbones, MinJS beat random selection, FwdJS usually surpassed the strongest baseline, and LogLin performed best, with the biggest gains on disagreement cases.
watch_item: The reverse posterior is weaker as a standalone predictor, so the approach depends on a good likelihood specification and may benefit from calibration when labeled data are available.
paper_title: When Agents Disagree: Bayesian Backward Reasoning as a Label-Free Anchor for Multi-Agent Collective Decision-Making
